- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or flat, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture mean reversion.
- After a price spike (forecast > 72.5), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +2.5% above peak or use 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1–2 days of upward bias in forecast tail.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply 1.5–2.5% upward bias for final 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.20 values, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; add 0.5–1.0% upward drift to forecast.
